name: Schema Design Conventions
description: This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on schema design so output stays consistent and easy to review.
content:
This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on schema design so output stays consistent and easy to review.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When schema design decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
2. Measure before optimizing any schema design bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
3. Check that schema design terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
4. Keep schema design outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
5. Prefer explicit, readable schema design solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
6. Re-check edge cases relevant to schema design (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
7. Validate schema design outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
8. When multiple schema design strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
9. Prefer the simplest schema design approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
10. Surface known limitations of a chosen schema design approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
11. Before starting schema design work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
12. Keep schema design changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not skip documenting schema design assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid mixing unrelated schema design concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not silently drop schema design edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these schema design guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
